what: Calculate prevalence and confidence intervals — calc_prevalence
title: Calculate prevalence and confidence intervals — calc_prevalence
text: Calculates survey-weighted prevalence estimates confidence intervals binary outcome single-year rolling multi-year periods. Different analysis populations can specified different outcomes denominator variable.

title: Calculate prevalence and confidence intervals — calc_prevalence
code: calc_prevalence(   data,   denominator,   year_var,   outcome_var,   weight_var = NULL,   psu = NULL,   strata = NULL,   by = NULL,   rolling_year = 1,   ci_level = 0.95,   digits = 1 )

title: Calculate prevalence and confidence intervals — calc_prevalence
text: data data frame data.table containing survey data. denominator Character string giving name binary denominator/eligibility variable. Observations denominator == 1 included analysis population; observations denominator == 0 excluded. denominator variable therefore defines population prevalence estimate applies. year_var Character string giving name variable containing calendar year. outcome_var Character string giving name binary outcome variable. outcome must coded 0 1, 1 indicates outcome interest. weight_var Character string giving name survey weight variable. NULL run uweighted prevalence. Default NULL. psu Optional character string giving name primary sampling unit (PSU) variable. NULL (default), ids = ~1 used clustering specified. strata Optional character string giving name survey stratum variable. NULL (default), stratification specified. Optional character vector giving names variables defining subgroups prevalence calculated. NULL, estimates calculated entire analysis population within rolling period. rolling_year Positive integer specifying number calendar years included rolling period. default 3. Use rolling_year = 1 calculate prevalence separately year. ci_level Numeric value 0 1 specifying confidence level confidence intervals. default 0.95. digits Number digits show prevalence. Default 1.

title: Calculate prevalence and confidence intervals — calc_prevalence
text: data frame containing prevalence estimates confidence intervals produced survey::svyby(). prevalence estimate survey-weighted mean outcome_var. 0/1 outcome equivalent prevalence. Confidence interval columns typically named ci.2.5 ci.97.5 95\

title: Calculate prevalence and confidence intervals — calc_prevalence
text: denominator argument defines analysis population selected outcome. observations denominator == 1 used prevalence calculation. allows different outcomes different eligible populations. example, one outcome may applicable entire survey population another may applicable particular age group eligible population. denominator variable applied missing outcomes removed, rolling periods constructed, survey design created. Therefore, denominator defines population prevalence variance estimated. survey design constructed using survey::svydesign(). psu supplied, ids = ~1 used, treating observations independent sampling units. psu supplied, used primary sampling unit. strata supplied, used account stratification. confidence intervals based survey-design variance estimator used survey::svymean() survey::svyby(). therefore different confidence intervals calculated using effective sample size, $$ SE = \sqrt{p(1-p)/n_{\mathrm{eff}}}, $$ $$ n_{\mathrm{eff}} = \frac{(\sum w_i)^2}{\sum w_i^2}. $$ PSU /strata information available original survey design, supplied allow variance estimator account complex sample design. Rolling rolling_years defined using calendar years. example, rolling_year = 3, estimate 2022 uses observations 2020 2022. rolling_year = 1, year treated estimation period. Note rolling periods overlap. example, observation 2020 can contribute 2018–2020, 2019–2021, 2020–2022 estimates. estimates overlapping periods therefore treated statistically independent. Missing values denominator treated eligible cause error analysis population determined. Observations missing values outcome_var removed contribute prevalence estimate. outcome must coded 0/1. outcome, survey-weighted mean prevalence outcome.

title: Calculate prevalence and confidence intervals — calc_prevalence
code: # Annual prevalence for an outcome with a specific denominator calc_prevalence(   data = dt,   denominator = "eligible",   year_var = "year",   outcome_var = "outcome",   weight_var = "weight",   rolling_year = 1 ) #> Error in calc_prevalence(data = dt, denominator = "eligible", year_var = "year",     outcome_var = "outcome", weight_var = "weight", rolling_year = 1): 'data' must be a data.frame or data.table.  # Three-year rolling prevalence calc_prevalence(   data = dt,   denominator = "eligible",   year_var = "year",   outcome_var = "outcome",   weight_var = "weight",   rolling_year = 3 ) #> Error in calc_prevalence(data = dt, denominator = "eligible", year_var = "year",     outcome_var = "outcome", weight_var = "weight", rolling_year = 3): 'data' must be a data.frame or data.table.  # Three-year rolling prevalence accounting for PSU and strata calc_prevalence(   data = dt,   denominator = "eligible",   year_var = "year",   outcome_var = "outcome",   weight_var = "weight",   psu = "psu",   strata = "stratum",   rolling_year = 3 ) #> Error in calc_prevalence(data = dt, denominator = "eligible", year_var = "year",     outcome_var = "outcome", weight_var = "weight", psu = "psu",     strata = "stratum", rolling_year = 3): 'data' must be a data.frame or data.table.  # Three-year rolling prevalence by region and gender calc_prevalence(   data = dt,   denominator = "eligible",   year_var = "year",   outcome_var = "outcome",   weight_var = "weight",   psu = "psu",   strata = "stratum",   by = c("region", "gender"),   rolling_year = 3 ) #> Error in calc_prevalence(data = dt, denominator = "eligible", year_var = "year",     outcome_var = "outcome", weight_var = "weight", psu = "psu",     strata = "stratum", by = c("region", "gender"), rolling_year = 3): 'data' must be a data.frame or data.table.

title: Create Cannabis Population Indicators — create_cann_pop
text: Creates binary population indicators based lifetime, last year, /last month substance use variables. function generates columns indicating whether individuals ever used, used past year, used past month. Users can specify indicators create.

title: Create Cannabis Population Indicators — create_cann_pop
code: create_cann_pop(dt, types = c("ltp", "lyp", "lmp"), vars, value = "cannabis")

title: Create Cannabis Population Indicators — create_cann_pop
text: dt data.table data.frame containing substance use variables. types character vector specifying indicators create. Must contain one : "ltp" (lifetime), "lyp" (last year), "lmp" (last month). Default c("ltp", "lyp", "lmp") create three indicators. order content types must match order content vars. vars character vector containing variable names corresponding types. types = "ltp", provide 1 variable (lifetime use) types = c("ltp", "lyp"), provide 2 variables (lifetime, last year) types = c("ltp", "lyp", "lmp"), provide 3 variables (lifetime, last year, last month) Variables coded 1-2 indicate use. value character string use suffix created variables. Default "cannabis".

title: Create Cannabis Population Indicators — create_cann_pop
text: data.table additional columns based types: ltpPop_{value} Lifetime population indicator (1 = ever used, 0 = never) lypPop_{value} Last year population indicator (1 = used past year, 0 = ) lmpPop_{value} Last month population indicator (1 = used past month, 0 = )

title: Create Cannabis Population Indicators — create_cann_pop
text: function creates cascading indicators: Lifetime (ltp): 1 lifetime use variable 1 2 Last year (lyp): 1 last year variable 1-2, lifetime variable 2 Last month (lmp): 1 last month variable 1-2, last year variable 2, lifetime variable 2 cascading logic means: create "lyp", must also include "ltp" types create "lmp", must also include "ltp" "lyp" types

title: Create Cannabis Population Indicators — create_cann_pop
text: input data.table copied avoid modifying reference. Missing values handled FALSE (coded 0) conditions.

title: Create Cannabis Population Indicators — create_cann_pop
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ library(data.table)  # Create sample data dt <- data.table(   id = 1:5,   lifetime_use = c(1, 2, 3, 1, NA),   year_use = c(1, 2, 3, 2, 1),   month_use = c(1, 3, 3, 1, 2) )  # Create all three indicators (default) result <- create_cann_pop(   dt = dt,   vars = c("can1", "can6", "can10"),   value = "cannabis" )  # Create only lifetime indicator result <- create_cann_pop(   dt = dt,   types = "ltp",   vars = "lifetime_use",   value = "cannabis" )  # Create lifetime and last year indicators result <- create_cann_pop(   dt = dt,   types = c("ltp", "lyp"),   vars = c("lifetime_use", "year_use"),   value = "cannabis" )  # With different substance result <- create_cann_pop(   dt = dt,   types = c("ltp", "lyp", "lmp"),   vars = c("can1", "can6", "can10"),   value = "mdma" ) } # }

title: Create Population Indicators for LTP and LYP Variables — create_narko_pop

title: Create Population Indicators for LTP and LYP Variables — create_narko_pop
text: d data.table data.frame. input dataset. types character vector specifying population types calculate. Options "ltp" /"lyp". Default c("ltp", "lyp"). vars named unnamed character vector variable names corresponding types. named, names match types. unnamed, order match order types. val character string used suffix created variable names. New variables named ltpPop_<val> /lypPop_<val>. ans character string specifying name answer/response column dataset ltp drug question. Default "ans1".

text: data.table new population indicator columns added. original data.table modified (copy made internally).

title: Create Population Indicators for LTP and LYP Variables — create_narko_pop
text: function creates population indicators based following logic: LTP: Value 1 LTP variable 1 2, LTP missing answer variable ans1 equals 2. Otherwise 0. LYP: Value 1 LYP variable 1 2, LYP missing LTP equals 2, LYP missing answer variable ans2 equals 2. Otherwise 0.

title: Create Population Indicators for LTP and LYP Variables — create_narko_pop
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ library(data.table)  # Create sample data dt <- data.table(   id = 1:5,   ltp_var = c(1, 2, NA, 3, NA),   lyp_var = c(1, NA, 2, NA, NA),   ans1 = c(1, 1, 2, 1, 2) )  # Calculate both LTP and LYP populations result <- narko_pop(   d = dt,   types = c("ltp", "lyp"),   vars = c("ltp_var", "lyp_var"),   val = "2024" )  # Calculate only LTP population result_ltp <- narko_pop(   d = dt,   types = "ltp",   vars = "ltp_var",   val = "2024" ) } # }

what: Categorize Age Variable into Groups — group_age

title: Categorize Age Variable into Groups — group_age
code: group_age(   dt,   var,   breaks,   labels = NULL,   new_var = NULL,   right = FALSE,   include.lowest = TRUE,   validate = TRUE,   copy = FALSE,   missing_values = NULL )

title: Categorize Age Variable into Groups — group_age
text: dt data.table. input data.table object containing age variable. var Character string. Name age variable categorized. breaks Numeric vector. Break points age categories. include minimum value ensure ages captured. labels Character vector, optional. Labels age groups. NULL, default labels generated automatically. Length one less number breaks. Default NULL. new_var Character string, optional. Name new categorical variable created. NULL, defaults "_group". Default NULL. right Logical. intervals closed right (open left) vice versa? Default FALSE. include.lowest Logical. lowest break point included first interval? Default TRUE. validate Logical. input validation performed? Default TRUE. copy Logical. copy data.table returned instead modifying place? TRUE object name different name. Default FALSE. missing_values Numeric vector, optional. Values treated missing (e.g., survey codes like 999 "know", 998 "answer"). values converted NA categorization. Default NULL.

title: Categorize Age Variable into Groups — group_age
text: modified data.table new age group variable added. copy=TRUE, returns new data.table; otherwise modifies input data.table reference.

title: Categorize Age Variable into Groups — group_age
text: function uses base R's cut() function internally create age categories. Common age groupings demographic analysis include: Younger: 0-18 years Young adult: 19-30 years Middle age: 31-50 years Older adult: 51+ years breaks vector always include minimum expected age (often 0) maximum value exceeds highest age data.

title: Categorize Age Variable into Groups — group_age
text: Survey data often uses special numeric codes represent different types missing responses: 999: "know" 998: "Prefer answer" 997: "applicable" -1, -9: Various missing codes missing_values parameter allows specify codes, converted NA age categorization. ensures survey response codes interfere legitimate age values properly treated missing data resulting age groups. validate=TRUE, function checks : Existence specified age variable Numeric age variable Proper breaks vector (numeric, sorted, minimum length 2) Matching labels length (provided) Coverage valid age values breaks (excluding missing codes) Valid missing_values parameter (provided)
